transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-03
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Gomez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Sam Lee (NovaHealth Platform Eng), Maya Ortiz (NovaHealth Product), Jordan Kim (NovaHealth Security), Leah Park (NovaHealth ML Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Quick status on provisioning and creds; staging runs completed with baseline latency but p99 spikes observed on long contexts.
- SE tuned batching and kv cache settings; quantization profile applied for lower memory.
- Security asked for KMS integration notes and SOC2 scope confirmation.
- Action items: bench traces, CIDR confirmation, security questionnaire, cost proposal for dedicated pilot.

Topics: onboarding progress; access setup; bench results (latency/cost); infra readiness; security gating; next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Gomez: Okay, cool, thanks everybody for joining. um we'll kick off, this is our weekly pilot sync, focus on where the environment is at and any final blockers. Priya you want to run quick status?
[00:18] Priya Shah: Yeah absolutely. So, we finished the staging runs last night. baseline throughput looks good for the 512 token flows, median latency around 70ms on our host, but the p95/p99 with 3–4k context got noisy. we think it's kv cache misses in the early steps plus some batching serialization.
[00:35] Sam Lee: I saw those numbers in the spreadsheet, thanks. the p99 jumped to like 2.1s on a 4k token job which is above our SLA target, that was the main concern for product.
[00:48] Maya Ortiz: Right, from product perspective the user experience needs to keep latents under 1s for interactive sessions, so p99s matter a lot.
[00:58] Priya Shah: Totally. so we did two things: 1) enabled prefix KV caching at the request gateway to reduce repeated context sends, and 2) adjusted continuous batching window down from 80ms to 40ms for low-latency paths. that dropped the median and p95 by about 30%, p99 improved but we still saw outliers when tails long.
[01:22] Leah Park: Do you think quantization played a role? we tested int8 last week. memory was fine but I worry about some accuracy vs perf tradeoffs.
[01:31] Priya Shah: Good call — we used an 8-bit quant profile optimized for throughput (profile B) — it saved memory and allowed larger batch sizes without OOMs but occasionally added slight generation stalls on very long context steps. we're going to run a mixed-precision pass (int8 for weights, fp16 for activations) next; that often smooths out the stall behavior.
[01:52] Jordan Kim: From security I'm tracking two things: KMS integration for customer-managed keys and audit log retention. can you confirm if Redwood's cloud natively supports our HSM provider? also SOC2 evidence for change management.
[02:05] Alex Gomez: Jordan, short answer: yes we integrate with common KMS providers, and we have an HSM workflow — I'll attach the KMS integration doc. SOC2 artifacts are in the security pack; we'll map which controls live in the private plane vs our hosted plane. I'll flag which items need joint attestation.
[02:28] Jordan Kim: OK please include the attestation details. we need to know which logs show API key usage per-token and whether there is a separate audit stream that we can forward into our SIEM.
[02:40] Priya Shah: We can emit audit logs to a customer-defined sink and we have token-level cost traces. forwarding to a SIEM is usually via an S3 export or syslog/forwarder — Sam, which would you prefer?
[02:54] Sam Lee: S3 export works best for us initially. we can pull into the SIEM from there.
[02:58] Alex Gomez: Noted. on the infra front, Priya, you mentioned gateway changes — any work left for NovaHealth infra?
[03:05] Priya Shah: There's one outstanding: we need the VPC peering CIDR confirmed so our gateway NAT rules won't conflict. Sam said he'd validate; once that's in we'll flip the peering and run end-to-end tests.
[03:18] Sam Lee: I'm on it. I'll confirm by Friday. Also I tried a cross-region sim and saw a 50–80ms bump when traffic crossed to our east region — is there an edge routing option?
[03:32] Alex Gomez: We can route to a closer Redwood region based on policy; for pilot we recommended keeping region local to reduce RTT. For production we can add a regional fallback policy.
[03:42] Maya Ortiz: Quick question on Dedicated vs Hosted: if we go Dedicated for the pilot, what's the ramp cost and how does burst capacity work?
[03:51] Alex Gomez: Good question. short: Dedicated gives you reserved throughput and isolation. burst is an add-on (policy can spill to hosted nodes when reserved pool saturated). cost wise I'll share a spreadsheet that models committed GPU hours vs metered hosted overflow; for small pilots Dedicated can be slightly more expensive but gives predictable latency.
[04:10] Leah Park: From ML side, we want to test model variants — slightly smaller 3B vs 7B family — to balance cost and latency. can Redwood host both and route by route?
[04:21] Priya Shah: Yep. routing by route and by model variant is supported. we can set automatic fallback to the smaller model when latency SLOs are about to breach. that's in the rollout policy configs.
[04:33] Sam Lee: On the bench trace attachments, I noticed some transcription artifacts in the CSV — like request ids missing. can you include raw logs?
[04:41] Priya Shah: We'll include full trace bundles (request_id, token-level timestamps, kernel queue wait times). the CSV is the summarized sheet but raw traces will be attached to the ticket.
[04:51] Jordan Kim: Also, about data residency — we need confirmation that logs and ephemeral context are cleared after 30 days and not persisted outside our region.
[05:00] Alex Gomez: For Private/VPC deployments we can ensure data residency and configurable retention. For hosted we can set retention policies and also offer a private control plane option if NovaHealth needs entire control.
[05:11] Maya Ortiz: If we do private control plane, how long is onboarding? we had a three-week constraint.
[05:16] Alex Gomez: Private control plane onboarding typically takes 4–6 weeks depending on network approvals; Dedicated (hosted reserved capacity) can start faster — usually within 7–10 days once contracts signed. for your three-week constraint we can probably do a hosted Dedicated pilot.
[05:32] Sam Lee: That works as a fallback. priority is to validate latency and the user flows.
[05:38] Priya Shah: For the technical tunings: we'll run the mixed-precision bench and a long-tail 4k token end-to-end test (this is the one that caused the p99). We'll also try a conservative KV warmup policy at session start to reduce cache misses.
[05:55] Leah Park: Can you remind us what the endpoint for KV warming will look like? we'd prefer not to add a big extra payload on start.
[06:03] Priya Shah: It's a lightweight sticky request, usually 2–4 tokens synthetic prompt to prime the KV. negligible cost and usually cuts the first long-step latency substantially.
[06:11] Maya Ortiz: Great. curious about cost impact — do you have rough delta for enabling warmups and smaller batching?
[06:18] Alex Gomez: Warmups add tiny token cost but can reduce retries and late penalties; the spreadsheet will show a modeled delta. smaller batching slightly increases per-token cost, but you can tune to hit a latency vs cost sweet spot.
[06:33] Sam Lee: On telemetry — we want per-route histograms and token-level breakdowns. will the console expose raw percentiles and traces?
[06:41] Priya Shah: Console shows per-route median/p95/p99 and has an option to download raw traces for a selected window. we also provide a daily aggregate and live stream option for debugging.
[06:53] Jordan Kim: Make sure the audit stream is separated and only accessible to our security group.
[06:58] Alex Gomez: Yep we'll set RBAC so only Jordan and her designees can access the audit export.
[07:05] Maya Ortiz: Any blockers on creds? we gave service account earlier but still seeing auth failures in staging.
[07:12] Priya Shah: We saw a token TTL mismatch; Sam you issued a short-lived key that expired mid-run. if you can reissue with the recommended TTL (12 hours for staging) we should be fine.
[07:23] Sam Lee: Reissuing now and will confirm.
[07:27] Alex Gomez: Good. let's run through the tentative timeline / milestones:
[07:31] Alex Gomez: - By 2027-02-05: Priya to share bench traces and mixed-precision run results.
[07:38] Alex Gomez: - By 2027-02-06: Sam confirms CIDR and reissues correct TTL creds.
[07:44] Alex Gomez: - By 2027-02-07: Jordan sends security questionnaire answers and approved KMS provider list.
[07:50] Alex Gomez: - By 2027-02-08: Alex to send Dedicated pilot cost proposal and recommended commit.
[07:56] Maya Ortiz: Can we get a short doc that maps our success criteria into test cases? e.g., p99 under 1s for 95% of interactive flows, cost per 1k tokens under X, etc.
[08:08] Alex Gomez: Absolutely. We'll map success criteria to bench cases and include acceptance thresholds.
[08:14] Leah Park: One minor thing — during one run we saw an unexpected kernel scheduling log noise; might be specific to the GPU driver version. is there a supported list?
[08:24] Priya Shah: We have a supported driver matrix; we'll attach that driver/OS compatibility matrix to the ticket. often mismatches cause jitter.
[08:34] Sam Lee: Sounds good. last question — any immediate risk that would block our go/no-go for next week's validation?
[08:41] Alex Gomez: Not a blocker. items are mitigations: CIDR confirm, reissued creds, bench traces. if those land on schedule we can validate next week.
[08:49] Maya Ortiz: ok let's recap and close.
[08:52] Alex Gomez: Recap: Priya runs the mixed-precision + 4k context bench and attaches raw traces; Sam confirms CIDR and TTL; Jordan provides security answers; Alex will prepare a Dedicated pilot cost model. We'll regroup same time next week unless an emergency pops up.
[09:08] Maya Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[09:11] Sam Lee: Thanks.
[09:13] Jordan Kim: bye.
